notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch of https://www.theone.com/en-ae/ (301s to bare https://www.theone.com/, Kartmax platform). No Claude-specific robots.txt disallow. 'New' is a top-level main-nav item (alongside Living/Dining/Bed & Bath/Lighting/Home Decor/Sale), landing at /category/new with an 'All New' alias at /category/new-all-new (same special-collection uuid 7087b6f7e47f820d, same rendered count -> true alias, kept /category/new as canonical since it's the actual nav-linked URL). Since the count/grid is filled client-side from the page's own request to engine.kartmax.in/api/fast/search/v1/<md5(theone.com)>/plp-special, verified with Playwright (JS render): page title 'Discover New Arrivals | Shop Latest Trends & Styles', h1='New', marketing copy 'Introducing our latest arrivals to elevate your home decor!... explore our new collections online and be the first to bring home the latest trends in home styling' - this is a genuine product-listing PLP (real grid, price-range/category filters, sort-by, in-stock filter) representing recently-added catalogue items, not an editorial/lookbook page, so it passes the brief's Collection-page test cleanly (no MANUAL REVIEW flag needed). Rendered #km-plp-count = '103', independently confirmed via the page's own API response (fieldspecials=_uuid~7087b6f7e47f820d) result.count=103. The site further exposes 5 genuine department-level children under New (Living, Dining, Bed & Bath, Lighting, Home Decor), each its own uuid-driven listing at /category/new-living, new-dining, new-bed-bath, new-lighting, new-home-decor, each verified the same way (rendered count + API result.count). Children sum exactly to the parent: 16+4+12+40+31=103, confirming a genuine non-overlapping department split (not an error/coincidence). No deeper leaf-level split (e.g. New Sofas) was recorded - the brief's example granularity is department-level (e.g. 'Furniture New Arrivals'), and going further would over-fragment the merchandising concept. Checked main nav mega-menus, footer, and sitemap.xml (1357 URLs) for other New-Arrivals-style terms (new in, just in, just arrived, latest, what's new, recently added) - found none beyond the New tree already captured. robots.txt disallows /search to crawlers so the on-site search box was not used; the fully enumerated New mega-menu plus sitemap coverage is sufficient here since a positive result was already found and confirmed. Site is English-only (html lang=en dir=ltr; /ar-ae/ returns HTTP 500), so no local-language nav check was applicable.
